title: Shadow runner: add alert rules + dashboard references (error rate, queue depth, drops)
author: Allison Grant
description: Context: Shadow Traffic runs must never impact primary responses, but we still need strong guardrails for the shadow execution path to prevent silent capacity leaks and to enable fast disablement when misconfigured. This PR adds Prometheus alert rules + dashboard wiring for the Shadow Runner service, focused on: (1) shadow execution error rate, (2) shadow queue depth / age, and (3) shadow drop counts (budget enforcement / backpressure). Alerts are explicitly scoped as shadow-only (non-paging where appropriate), and include runbook + dashboard links for on-call. Changes: - Adds new alert rules under shadow_runner.* with separate severities for WARN vs PAGE. - Adds multi-window burn-style alerting for sustained queue depth (PAGE only when backed up long enough to risk masking widespread failures). - Adds drop-count alerts keyed off drop_reason (sampled / budget_exceeded / queue_full / disabled) with guardrails to avoid cardinality blow-ups. - Wires dashboards: adds links to the SRE overview dashboard panels (Shadow Evals / Shadow Runner) and points alerts to the canonical Grafana dashboards + Loki queries. - Adds a small README snippet documenting expected semantics: drops are acceptable when budget-limited, but sudden deltas relative to baseline should be investigated. Notes/assumptions: - Alerts are tied to the aggregated shadow_eval metrics (no per-request IDs). - Thresholds are conservative for beta: queue depth paging requires sustained backlog and elevated drop rate, not just transient spikes. - All alerts include a first step to verify kill switch state + current sampling policy, since misconfig is a common failure mode. Testing: - Unit: rule lint via promtool; CI checks validate YAML schema and label allowlist usage. - Manual: verified panels render in staging Grafana; simulated queue backlog in staging by setting shadow_runner.max_inflight=0 and confirmed alert evaluation + links. Rollout: safe to merge; alert rules are behind the shadow_runner alerts folder which is only enabled in beta envs today (prod enablement is controlled by SRE config).
commits: observability: add shadow runner alert rules for queue depth / error rate
dashboards: wire shadow runner panels into SRE overview + add annotation links
alerts: add drop_count alerts with drop_reason allowlist + docs
chore: promtool lint + CI wiring for new alert files
review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: Can we avoid paging on shadow error rate alone? In beta we saw elevated shadow errors during capacity constraints; I’d rather PAGE on a combination of sustained queue depth + sustained drops (queue_full/budget_exceeded) and keep error_rate as WARN unless it’s extreme.

Allison Grant (author): Agreed. Updated: error_rate is WARN at >2% for 10m, PAGE only at >15% for 10m *and* shadow_queue_depth above threshold. Also added annotations in the alert description to call out shadow-only impact.
Logan Wright: Please confirm drop_reason is constrained to an allowlist. We can’t afford arbitrary strings here (cardinality). Also, is request_route included anywhere in these alerts?

Allison Grant (author): Drop reasons are explicitly enumerated in telemetry/tag_allowlists/shadow_eval_tags.yaml. Alerts use aggregated series only (no request_route label). Route-level breakdown stays in dashboards with bucketed route_group (per ENG-2435).

Rafael Mendes: Runbook link is good, but I want the alert to include the exact Loki query we use for ‘shadow runner disabled’ and ‘budget exceeded’ confirmations. On-call tends to copy/paste from the alert.
Allison Grant (author): Added Loki query snippets to alert annotations + updated runbooks/shadow_runner.md with a dedicated “Alert quick triage” section.

Caleb Johnson: Minor: the alert name shadow_runner_queue_age_seconds is misleading; it’s derived from queue depth + ingest timestamp. Can we call it queue_delay_seconds and document the approximation?
Allison Grant (author): Renamed metric reference to shadow_runner_queue_delay_seconds in dashboards/alerts and added a comment that it’s approximate (time in queue based on enqueue_ts histogram).
Sean Gallagher: Looks good. Please ensure routing in Alertmanager goes to shadow-traffic channel first (not paging) for WARN. PAGE should go through standard SRE paging policy.
Allison Grant (author): Confirmed. Updated alertmanager route labels: severity=warn -> #shadow-traffic-ops, severity=page -> pager + #sre-oncall.
release_notes: Added shadow runner alerts for error rate, queue backlog/delay, and drops with runbook + dashboard links.
Alert routing separates shadow-only WARN signals from paging conditions to avoid noisy on-call.
